Format count and percentage pairs

Source: R/n_pct.r
ks_n_pct.Rd

Produces formatted "n (xx.x%)" strings from absolute counts and denominators. An S3 generic dispatching on the class of n:

  • numeric method — formats a single vector of counts.

  • data.frame method — formats one or more named count columns inside a data.frame or tibble simultaneously, leaving all other columns unchanged.

Usage

ks_n_pct(n, totals, na.rep = NA_character_)

Arguments

n

Numeric (integer) vector of counts, or a data.frame / tibble whose named columns contain counts.

totals

Numeric denominator(s).

  • numeric method: a scalar or a numeric vector recycled against n.

  • data.frame method: a named numeric vector whose names must match column names present in n.

na.rep

Replacement string for NA counts.

  • NA_character_ (default): propagate NA in the output.

  • Any character string, e.g. "" or "0 (\ 0.0%)": substitute missing counts with that string.

Value

  • numeric method: a character vector of the same length as n.

  • data.frame method: the input data.frame with the named count columns replaced by formatted character strings; all other columns are unchanged.

Details

Counts are converted to integer before formatting so that both integer and whole-number double vectors are accepted.

Percentages are formatted as "%5.1f%%", giving one decimal place and a minimum field width of 5 characters (e.g. " 5.0%", "100.0%"). The fixed width ensures vertical alignment when columns are printed side-by-side.

A warning is issued when any element of totals is zero, as this produces Inf in the percentage.

Examples

## Numeric method — single total
ks_n_pct(c(10L, 20L, 30L), 56L)
#> [1] "10 ( 17.9%)" "20 ( 35.7%)" "30 ( 53.6%)"

## Numeric method — element-wise totals
ks_n_pct(c(10L, 20L, 30L), c(34L, 42L, 56L))
#> [1] "10 ( 29.4%)" "20 ( 47.6%)" "30 ( 53.6%)"

## NA propagation (default)
ks_n_pct(c(10L, NA_integer_, 30L), 50L)
#> [1] "10 ( 20.0%)" NA            "30 ( 60.0%)"

## Replace NA with an explicit string
ks_n_pct(c(10L, NA_integer_, 30L), 50L, na.rep = "0 (  0.0%)")
#> [1] "10 ( 20.0%)" "0 (  0.0%)"  "30 ( 60.0%)"

## Replace NA with an empty string
ks_n_pct(c(10L, NA_integer_, 30L), 50L, na.rep = "")
#> [1] "10 ( 20.0%)" ""            "30 ( 60.0%)"

## data.frame method
dex <- data.frame(
  par       = c("A", "B", "C"),
  Therapy_A = c(11L, 23L, 14L),
  Therapy_B = c(20L,  1L, NA_integer_)
)
ks_n_pct(dex, c(Therapy_A = 56L, Therapy_B = 67L))
#>   par   Therapy_A   Therapy_B
#> 1   A 11 ( 19.6%) 20 ( 29.9%)
#> 2   B 23 ( 41.1%)  1 (  1.5%)
#> 3   C 14 ( 25.0%)        <NA>

## data.frame method — keep only one column
ks_n_pct(dex, c(Therapy_A = 56L))
#>   par   Therapy_A Therapy_B
#> 1   A 11 ( 19.6%)        20
#> 2   B 23 ( 41.1%)         1
#> 3   C 14 ( 25.0%)        NA
